name: Permanent Resident Status -- Marriage to a Citizen

qualifying_event.description: The spouse of a Trinidad and Tobago citizen may, after a sustained period of lawful residence on a spousal entry permit, apply for permanent resident status.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Marriage certificate; entry permits covering the full residence period; evidence of cohabitation and genuine relationship.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires marriage to a Trinidad and Tobago citizen and a spousal entry permit -- marriage alone does not confer permanent residence.
Requires approximately 3 to 5 years of continuous lawful residence as the spouse of the citizen, per established administrative practice (no fixed statutory minimum).
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate continuous, unbroken residence as the spouse, documented with valid entry permits throughout.

evidence_required.document: Character certificates (T&T and country of origin)
Entry permits covering the full residence period
Evidence of cohabitation and financial self-sufficiency

sources.title: Martin George & Company -- Permanent Resident Status Through Marriage to a Trinidad and Tobago Citizen: Immigration Act Chapter 18:01 Section 10, ministerial discretion with no reasons required, 3-5 year administrative-practice residence expectation

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Trinidad and Tobago's initial build. STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced only to a tier-3 law firm article; no fixed statutory residence minimum exists per the source itself, only administrative practice, and no gov.tt page was found confirming this specific figure. IMPORTANT CITATION CONFLICT: this article and the tier-3 article underlying tt_permanent_residence_general.json both cite 'Section 10' of the Immigration Act but describe it as governing two different things (this article: ministerial discretion to grant marriage-based PR; the other article: the 'prohibited immigrants' classification used as a disqualifying ground for the 5-year route) -- this inconsistency was not resolved against the Act's primary text in this pass (unlike the Citizenship Act, whose primary text was directly retrieved for tt_naturalisation.json and related files) and is flagged rather than silently picked one way. citizenship_after_months (60) mirrors the same 5-years-after-PR naturalisation rule used in tt_permanent_residence_general.json. Separately, the same source states citizenship may also become available via 'registration after 7 years of marriage' -- this claim directly conflicts with the primary Citizenship Act text reviewed for this build, which explicitly states marriage is NOT an independent registration ground (see tt_naturalisation.json's notes) -- that specific claim is NOT modelled as its own route here or elsewhere in this build precisely because of that conflict with primary legislation; disclosed in the chat summary rather than built as a route.
